evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.3: nōtus mihi nōmine tantum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: After the word it limits. Strengthened, tantummodo: velīs tantummodo, you have only to want it (Hor. S. 1.9.54, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Amph. 674: Sequere hāc mē modo
Cic. Fam. 16.11.1: modo fac, nē quid aliud cūrēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The “just” of requests: Properā modo, just hurry (Plaut. Men. 215). With numbers: semel modo, only once (Plaut. Poen. 1.3.30, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.22: nōn nōbīs sōlum nātī sumus
terms.comment: Mostly in nōn sōlum … sed etiam, not only … but also; on its own it is rarer (Lewis & Short). Sōlummodo is late.

terms.gloss: only, merely; at least as far as … goes
terms.grammar: adverb, after the word it limits
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.3 fin.: nōs animō dumtaxat vigēmus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. N. D. 2.47: sint ista pulchriōra dumtaxat aspectū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to this extent, so far”: it limits what goes before, animō dumtaxat, in spirit only. A word of prose, rarer than tantum and modo.

phrases.latin: nōn amō tē, Sabidī, nec possum dīcere quārē: hoc tantum possum dīcere, nōn amō tē
phrases.english: I don’t like you, Sabidius, and I can’t say why: all I can say is this, I don’t like you

phrases.latin: Sequere hāc mē modo … nē timē.
phrases.english: Just follow me this way … don’t be afraid.
we are not born for ourselves alone
